To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) multivariate autoregressions can be used to extract features from EEG that are useful for classification of mental tasks; (2) multivariate autogressive features are more useful than scalar autoregressive features; (3) the multivariate autoregression features are more useful for classification of EEG than are the eigenvalues and Karhunen-Love features; (4) neural networks trained via back-propagation can classify mental task EEG signals using multivariate autoregressor features

the use of multivariate autoregreesive models for the classification of spontaneous electroenephalographic signals during mental task is feasible and that the use of such models is a viable method for the classification of such signals.
multivariate autoregreesive models can be used to extract features for the classification of spontaneous electro-encephalographic data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of multichannel, non-invasive electroencephalography (EEG) to control a device, such as a wheelchair, by means of mental effort.
the use of EEG signals to allow paralyzed persons control of a device such as an artificial arm or a computer mouse.
the feasibility of using electroencephalography (EEG) to allow paralyzed persons control of a device such as an electric wheelchair.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the multivariate autoregression model is the most promising method for feature extraction from the EEG.
multivariate AR models are the most appropriate for EEG classification, but that scalar models are also a viable alternative.
the multivariate autoregression is an effective method for extracting features from the EEG for use in classification tasks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the EEG signals from the four subjects were successfully classified with an average accuracy of 90.8% on the trained set and 91.4 % on the untrained set.
we have developed a method that can be used to classify spontaneous EEG signals with an average accuracy of 90% or higher.
multivariate AR models can be successfully used to extract information from EEG signals that allows the classification of mental tasks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of AR models to extract features for EEG signal classification is feasible and that multivariate AR models may provide a more robust representation for classification.
the use of multivariate AR models to extract features for classification of EEG is a viable approach to developing a brain-computer interface for persons with severe motor disabilities.
multivariate autoregressions can be used for the classification of EEG signals with a classification accuracy of 90-95% and can be used for real-time classification of EEG.
